claim: APEX is an ascorbate peroxidase derived from soybean.
source: APEX, a modified ascorbate peroxidase derived from soybean, is a simple highly versatile marker for EM detection.
evidence: This is stated directly in the manuscript text as established knowledge about APEX.

claim: APEX has been used for detection of fusion proteins in cells, Drosophila, zebrafish, and mice.
source: The wide applicability of its use is demonstrated by studies utilizing APEX and its derivative, APEX2, for detection of fusion proteins in cells, Drosophila, zebrafish, and mice (Ariotti et al., 2015; Hirabayashi et al., 2018; Li et al., 2020; Meiring et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior work demonstrating APEX use in various organisms.

claim: APEX has been combined with nanobody-based detection systems for rapid localization of GFP- and mCherry-tagged proteins.
source: APEX has also been combined with nanobody-based detection systems for rapid localization of GFP- and mCherry-tagged proteins (Ariotti et al., 2015; Ariotti et al., 2018), and used to detect protein interactions using split GFP and nanobodies or using a novel split-APEX system (Ariotti et al., 2018; Han et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The diffuse DAB reaction product can make distinguishing the APEX reaction from electron-dense cellular components difficult.
source: Despite its versatility, the relatively diffuse diaminobenzidine (DAB) reaction product can make distinguishing the APEX reaction from electron-dense cellular components difficult and often requires an expert to interpret the images.
evidence: This is a stated limitation of existing APEX methods based on the authors' experience and knowledge.

claim: The APEX-Gold method converts the DAB reaction product into a silver/gold particle.
source: Here, we describe a simple method, APEX-Gold, which converts the diffuse oxidized diaminobenzidine reaction product of APEX into a silver/gold particle akin to that used for immunogold labelling.
evidence: This is the primary claim of the manuscript describing the new method.

claim: The APEX-Gold method increases the signal-to-noise ratio for EM detection.
source: The method increases the signal-to-noise ratio for EM detection, providing unambiguous detection of the tagged protein, and creates a readily quantifiable particulate signal.
evidence: This is a stated benefit of the method, supported by the experimental data shown in the figures.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can be combined with fast freezing and freeze substitution.
source: The method can be combined with different EM techniques including fast freezing and freeze substitution, focussed ion beam scanning EM, and electron tomography.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D,E.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can be combined with focussed ion beam scanning EM.
source: The method can be combined with different EM techniques including fast freezing and freeze substitution, focussed ion beam scanning EM, and electron tomography.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can be combined with electron tomography.
source: The method can be combined with different EM techniques including fast freezing and freeze substitution, focussed ion beam scanning EM, and electron tomography.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1F.

claim: Cell-free expression system membrane vesicles possess a defined quantum of signal that can act as an internal standard.
source: Quantitation of expressed APEX-fusion proteins is achievable using membrane vesicles generated by a cell-free expression system. These membrane vesicles possess a defined quantum of signal, which can act as an internal standard for determination of the absolute density of expressed APEX-fusion proteins.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally using CAV1-APEX2 vesicles in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The APEX-Gold method has high sensitivity for detecting fusion proteins expressed at low levels in CRISPR-edited mice.
source: Detection of fusion proteins expressed at low levels in cells from CRISPR-edited mice demonstrates the high sensitivity of the APEX-Gold method.
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally with Tpm3.1-APEX2 mice in Figure 2C-F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The optimal APEX-Gold protocol uses a modified Ag/Au enhancement method similar to that used to visualize luminal APEX.
source: The optimal protocol which satisfied these criteria was a modified Ag/Au enhancement method (Sedmak et al., 2009) as shown schematically in Figure 1A, similar to that used to visualize luminal APEX (Mavlyutov et al., 2017).
evidence: The protocol is based on a cited method and adapted for this application.

claim: The APEX-Gold method produces gold particles in the range of 10-15 nm in diameter.
source: This resulted in local production of stabilized gold particles in the range of 10–15 nm in diameter as the argyrophilic oxidized DAB reaction product converts the metal salts to colloidal particles at the site of the fusion protein.
evidence: This is a measured characteristic of the method.

claim: Gum arabic was included to provide consistent uniform nucleation.
source: Gum arabic was included to provide consistent uniform nucleation.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological choice based on established knowledge of gum arabic's function.

claim: Untransfected cells show negligible Ag/Au particles.
source: Untransfected cells show negligible Ag/Au particles (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A showing specificity of the method.

claim: Labelling is tightly restricted to caveolae with an average of 18.4 nm from the caveolar membrane to the centre of the particulate reaction product.
source: labelling is tightly restricted to caveolae with an average of 18.4 nm from the caveolar membrane to the centre of the particulate reaction product when imaged using transmission EM (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a measured resolution of the method for Cavin4-APEX2.

claim: The APEX-Gold method has been used successfully in over 20 different biological replicate experiments.
source: The method has been used successfully in over 20 different biological replicate experiments using the Cavin4-APEX2 and LifeAct-APEX2 systems.
evidence: This is a statement about the reproducibility of the method based on the authors' experimental experience.

claim: The APEX-Gold method results in an unambiguous particulate reaction product that is clearly definable without expert interpretation.
source: Critically, it results in an unambiguous particulate reaction product that is clearly definable without expert interpretation.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the method, supported by the clarity of labeling in the figures.

claim: APEX-Gold labelling is compatible with on-grid staining.
source: However, visualization of the electron-dense APEX-Gold particles is readily compatible with on-grid staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: APEX-Gold labelling can be visualized with Tokuyasu-cryosectioned samples.
source: We were also able to visualize APEX-Gold labelling with Tokuyasu-cryosectioned samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–C).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–C.

claim: The clarity and density of the APEX-Gold enhanced particulate signal makes the method compatible with 3D EM methods including 3D electron tomography.
source: The clarity and density of the APEX-Gold enhanced particulate signal makes the method compatible with 3D EM methods including 3D electron tomography (Figure 1F)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1F.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is compatible with array tomography scanning EM.
source: The clarity and density of the APEX-Gold enhanced particulate signal makes the method compatible with 3D EM methods including 3D electron tomography (Figure 1F), array tomography scanning EM (SEM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D,E)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 3D,E.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is compatible with focussed ion beam (FIB) EM.
source: The clarity and density of the APEX-Gold enhanced particulate signal makes the method compatible with 3D EM methods including 3D electron tomography (Figure 1F), array tomography scanning EM (SEM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D,E), focussed ion beam (FIB) EM (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is compatible with serial block-face SEM.
source: The clarity and density of the APEX-Gold enhanced particulate signal makes the method compatible with 3D EM methods including 3D electron tomography (Figure 1F), array tomography scanning EM (SEM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3D,E), focussed ion beam (FIB) EM (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B), and serial block-face SEM (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The gold particles can be resolved by supervised and automated segmentation.
source: The gold particles can also be resolved by supervised and automated segmentation (Weka Image J/FIJI plug-in, Figure 1—figure supplement 4B',C').
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B',C'.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is compatible with freeze substitution/low temperature embedding.
source: We also tested the compatibility of the method with freeze substitution/low temperature embedding (Figure 1—figure supplement 4D,E).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 1—figure supplement 4D,E.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can be combined with double labelling where the APEX-fusion protein is expressed endogenously and sections are labelled for other proteins of interest.
source: This makes APEX-Gold potentially compatible with double labelling, with the APEX-fusion protein being expressed endogenously in the cells and then sections labelled for other proteins of interest.
evidence: This is an inference based on the compatibility with freeze substitution and low temperature embedding.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is simple to use in CLEM approaches.
source: The APEX-Gold method is also simple to use in CLEM approaches (Figure 2C–F)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 2C–F.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can be checked by dot blot in parallel to the EM experiment.
source: The APEX-Gold method is also simple to use in CLEM approaches (Figure 2C–F) and can be checked by dot blot in parallel to the EM experiment to ensure the protocol is standardized (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; see Materials and methods for a standard protocol).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Mammalian caveolin-1 (CAV1) can generate nanovesicles with a defined number of caveolin proteins when expressed in a cell-free system.
source: We made use of the ability of mammalian caveolin-1 (CAV1), the major structural protein of caveolae, to generate nanovesicles with a defined number of caveolin proteins when expressed in a cell-free system (Jung et al., 2018)
evidence: This is based on a cited prior study.

claim: Cell-free synthesized GFP-CAV1-APEX2 vesicles contain approximately 110 GFP-CAV1-APEX2 molecules per vesicle.
source: The resulting vesicles contained a quantum of fluorescence consistent with approximately 110 GFP-CAV1-APEX2 molecules per vesicle.
evidence: This is determined by FCS analysis as described in the methods and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell-free synthesized APEX2 fusion protein had higher activity per µg of protein than commercial HRP preparation.
source: The cell-free synthesized APEX2 fusion protein had higher activity per µg of protein than the commercial HRP preparation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally by dot blot comparison in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Enhancement of the signal using the APEX-Gold protocol caused a slight increase in sensitivity of detection and a colour change in the dot blot.
source: Enhancement of the signal using the APEX-Gold protocol caused a slight increase in sensitivity of detection and a colour change in the dot blot providing a simple assay to check for successful enhancement.
evidence: Observed in the dot blot experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: An average of 16.9 Ag/Au particles per vesicle was observed in approximately 100-nm-thick sections of GFP-CAV1-APEX2 vesicles.
source: Under these enhancement conditions, an average of 16.9 Ag/Au particles per vesicle (mean ± 4.3 SD, n = 26) was observed in the approximately 100-nm-thick section.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: A varied distribution of gold sizes is hypothesized to be a consequence of fusion of multiple individual particulates into a single APEX-Gold product.
source: We observed a varied distribution of gold sizes which we hypothesize are a consequence of fusion of multiple individual particulates into a single APEX-Gold product (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on observations of the data.

claim: A low abundance antigen might be detected with high efficiency if the APEX2-tagged proteins are well spaced.
source: We speculated that a low abundance antigen might be detected with high efficiency if the APEX2-tagged proteins are well spaced.
evidence: This is a speculation that led to testing with tropomyosin.

claim: APEX-tagged tropomyosin is a good candidate to obtain precise physical organization because it is an extended molecule (~35 nm).
source: APEX-tagged tropomyosin is a good candidate to obtain precise physical organization because it is an extended molecule (~35 nm; Sousa et al., 2010)
evidence: This is based on cited knowledge about tropomyosin structure.

claim: In Tpm3.1-APEX2 heterozygous mice, expression of the fusion protein is lower than that of the endogenous Tpm3.1 protein (~5%).
source: Western blotting of mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) prepared from Tpm3.1-APEX2 heterozygous mice showed that expression of the fusion protein is lower than that of the endogenous Tpm3.1 protein (~5%; Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: Light microscopic studies of Tpm3.1-APEX2 MEFs revealed that specific labelling was associated with putative stress fibres.
source: Light microscopic studies revealed that specific labelling was associated with putative stress fibres (Figure 2C)
evidence: Demonstrated experimentally in Figure 2C.

claim: Correlative EM of Tpm3.1-APEX2 MEFs showed a dense and highly specific particulate labelling associated with bundles of actin, with an average of 10.6 nm from the particle to the centre of bundle mass.
source: this was confirmed by correlative EM (Figure 2D–F) that showed a dense and highly specific particulate labelling associated with bundles of actin, with an average of 10.6 nm from the particle to the centre of bundle mass when imaged using transmission EM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–F).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data shown in Figure 2D–F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–F.

claim: Particulate labelling in Tpm3.1-APEX2 MEFs was more uniform in size distribution compared to CAV1-APEX vesicles.
source: In addition, particulate labelling was more uniform in size distribution compared to CAV1-APEX vesicles and followed distinct tracks suggestive of individual actin filaments (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–F).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the experimental data.

claim: The greater uniformity of the gold reaction product in the Tpm.3.1-APEX2 MEFs suggests that the packing or density of tags may impact gold size distribution.
source: Moreover, the greater uniformity of the gold reaction product in the Tpm.3.1-APEX2 MEFs suggests that the packing or density of tags may impact gold size distribution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the results of different experiments.

claim: The APEX-Gold technique is powerful for detecting proteins at low expression levels and/or proteins expressed from endogenous loci.
source: These results clearly demonstrate the power of the APEX-Gold technique for detecting proteins at low expression levels and/or proteins expressed from endogenous loci.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Tpm3.1-APEX2 experiments.

claim: The APEX-Gold method has high resolution, low background, and is sensitive enough to detect proteins expressed at or below endogenous levels.
source: Here, we present a simple technique for identification of a protein of interest by transmission EM using a genetic tag to generate a particulate signal. The method has high resolution, low background, and is sensitive enough to detect proteins expressed at or below endogenous levels.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is compatible with 3D EM techniques such as serial block-face SEM, array tomography, FIB SEM, and electron tomography.
source: We provide a defined standard for calibration to ensure reproducibility and show that the method is compatible with 3D EM techniques such as serial block-face SEM, array tomography, FIB SEM, and electron tomography.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental demonstrations in the figures.

claim: The APEX system has been extended to new modifications including nanobody-based detection of fluorescent proteins and protein complexes.
source: The original APEX system involving a fusion with the protein of interest has been extended to new modifications including nanobody-based detection of fluorescent proteins and protein complexes and a split-APEX which only yields an active enzyme if brought together by two partner proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about APEX system developments.

claim: All APEX modifications are compatible with the APEX-Gold method for conversion of DAB to an Ag/Au particle.
source: All of these applications are compatible with the APEX-Gold method for conversion of DAB to an Ag/Au particle.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of the APEX-Gold method.

claim: The APEX-Gold method should be used in parallel to light microscopy as an initial step in protein localization.
source: The APEX-Gold method is so simple that it should be used in parallel to light microscopy as an initial step in protein localization.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the simplicity and utility of the method.

claim: Through the use of nanobody-APEX constructs, a co-transfection with a GFP-tagged protein can yield CLEM images in a very short timeframe.
source: In fact, through the use of nanobody-APEX constructs, a co-transfection with a GFP-tagged protein can yield CLEM images in a very short timeframe.
evidence: This is an inference about the potential application of the method.

claim: The APEX-Gold technique produces a particulate signal which is clearly distinguished from any cellular feature and is readily quantitated.
source: The technique produces a particulate signal which is clearly distinguished from any cellular feature and is readily quantitated.
evidence: This is supported by the experimental data showing clear particulate signals.

claim: By combining with an APEX-fusion protein of known signal density, it is possible to quantitatively compare particle density to antigen density.
source: By combining with an APEX-fusion protein of known signal density (here demonstrated by cell-free generated vesicle of a defined APEX density as a calibration standard), it is possible to quantitatively compare particle density to antigen density.
evidence: This is demonstrated with the CAV1-APEX2 vesicle experiments.

claim: An APEX-tagged antigen generated by CRISPR technology that is present at known density in a specific region of the cell could be used as a standard.
source: While we demonstrated this principle by using exogenously added cell-free synthesized caveolin-AP vesicles, an APEX-tagged antigen generated by CRISPR technology that is present at known density in a specific region of the cell could also be used as a standard.
evidence: This is a proposed alternative approach based on the demonstrated principle.

claim: Tpm3.1 is expressed at a concentration of 30 µM.
source: Tpm3.1 is expressed at a concentration of 30 µM (Meiring et al., 2018)
evidence: This is cited from a prior study.

claim: 5% of 30 µM Tpm3.1 represents a concentration of 1.5 µM.
source: Tpm3.1 is expressed at a concentration of 30 µM (Meiring et al., 2018) and so 5% represents a concentration of 1.5 µM.
evidence: This is a simple calculation based on the cited concentration.

claim: 1.5 µM Tpm3.1-APEX2 equates to a cellular copy number of approximately 1 million Tpm3.1 homodimers per cell.
source: This equates to a cellular Tpm3.1-APEX2 copy number of approximately 1 million Tpm3.1 homodimers per cell with 250,000 predicted to be associated with actin and the remainder cytosolic (Meiring et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the concentration and cited information.

claim: 250,000 Tpm3.1 homodimers are predicted to be associated with actin and the remainder cytosolic.
source: This equates to a cellular Tpm3.1-APEX2 copy number of approximately 1 million Tpm3.1 homodimers per cell with 250,000 predicted to be associated with actin and the remainder cytosolic (Meiring et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from a prior study.

claim: The level of Tpm3.1-APEX2 expression resulted in an excellent signal-to-noise ratio for the APEX-Gold particles on actin filaments.
source: This level of expression resulted in an excellent signal-to-noise ratio for the APEX-Gold particles on actin filaments, facilitated by the spacing of the gold along the filaments which is related to the size and organization of the tropomyosin oligomers.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The spacing of gold along actin filaments is related to the size and organization of the tropomyosin oligomers.
source: This level of expression resulted in an excellent signal-to-noise ratio for the APEX-Gold particles on actin filaments, facilitated by the spacing of the gold along the filaments which is related to the size and organization of the tropomyosin oligomers.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed pattern of labeling.

claim: The APEX-Gold method demonstrates remarkable efficiency of antigen detection.
source: This demonstrates the remarkable efficiency of antigen detection and lays the foundation for truly quantitative immuno-EM in cells and tissues for the first time.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful detection of low-abundance Tpm3.1-APEX2.

claim: APEX-Gold represents a significant advance in protein distribution analysis by EM.
source: APEX-Gold represents a significant advance in protein distribution analysis by EM.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the impact of the method.

claim: Compared with current APEX methods which rely on subjective interpretation of a diffuse DAB reaction product, the improved signal-to-noise ratio and a particulate, quantitative readout indicate that APEX-Gold should become the gold standard for localization of genetically tagged proteins in EM.
source: Compared with current APEX methods which rely on subjective interpretation of a diffuse DAB reaction product, the improved signal-to-noise ratio and a particulate, quantitative readout indicate that this method should become the gold standard for localization of genetically tagged proteins in EM.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the significance of the method based on its advantages.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is based on well-established methods for histological and EM visualization of the insoluble DAB product of peroxidase.
source: The method used here, which we have optimized for APEX localization, is based on well-established methods for histological and EM visualization of the insoluble DAB product of peroxidase (Adams, 1981; Danscher and Nörgaard, 1983; Dobó et al., 2011; Newman and Jasani, 1998; Pohl and Stierhof, 1998)
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: The APEX-Gold method is combined with methods of silver reduction and gold toning developed for photography in the 19th century.
source: The method used here, which we have optimized for APEX localization, is based on well-established methods for histological and EM visualization of the insoluble DAB product of peroxidase (Adams, 1981; Danscher and Nörgaard, 1983; Dobó et al., 2011; Newman and Jasani, 1998; Pohl and Stierhof, 1998), combined with the methods of silver reduction and gold toning developed for photography in the 19th century (for review, see Ellis, 1975).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a review.

claim: Silver/gold enhancement methods have been developed to allow enhancement of the DAB reaction for light microscopic applications.
source: These methods have been developed and used in many laboratories to allow enhancement of the DAB reaction for light microscopic applications, for converting the DAB signal to an easily detected particulate marker to allow discrimination from any cellular structures, and to increase the sensitivity of DAB detection (Dobó et al., 2011; Newman et al., 1983; Sedmak et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: The three principle steps of the APEX-Gold method involve: (1) production of the polymerized DAB product, (2) the reduction of silver ions to submicroscopic metallic silver by the argyrophilic DAB polymer, and (3) substitution of metallic silver by gold (gold toning).
source: The three principle steps involve: (1) production of the polymerized DAB product, (2) the reduction of silver ions to submicroscopic metallic silver by the argyrophilic DAB polymer, and (3) substitution of metallic silver by gold (gold toning), through the simple reaction Ag + Au+→ Ag++ Au to produce the more inert gold particle that can resist subsequent osmium treatment.
evidence: This describes the mechanistic steps of the method.

claim: Gum arabic was introduced for gold enhancement to allow precise control of Ag/Au nucleation and more uniform particle generation.
source: A further refinement is the use of gum arabic which was introduced for gold enhancement by Danscher, 1981; Danscher and Nörgaard, 1983 to allow precise control of Ag/Au nucleation and more uniform particle generation.
evidence: This is stated with citations to prior work.

claim: It is necessary to precisely control the development time for particulate deposition with the silver enhancement and subsequent gold toning.
source: First, it is necessary to take care to precisely control the development time for particulate deposition with the silver enhancement and subsequent gold toning.
evidence: This is a stated methodological consideration.

claim: Increased development times can increase the particle size, facilitating their identification, but can cause appearance of artefactual self-nucleated particles at sites lacking APEX.
source: Increased development times can increase the particle size, facilitating their identification, but can cause appearance of artefactual self-nucleated particles at sites lacking APEX (hence the need for careful control experiments).
evidence: This is a stated caveat based on experimental observations.

claim: Increased enhancement times can cause more variable particle size including the appearance of 'fused' gold particles where individual APEX molecules are closely packed.
source: Increased enhancement times can also cause more variable particle size including the appearance of 'fused' gold particles where individual APEX molecules are closely packed and so not clearly resolved as individual gold particles after enhancement (see for example Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a stated caveat with reference to experimental data.

claim: Fused gold particles can cause potential difficulties for quantitation and for applications in double labelling.
source: This can cause potential difficulties for quantitation and for applications in double labelling, for example, when the APEX-Gold method is combined with on-section labelling of Tokuyasu sections or freeze-substituted Lowicryl sections.
evidence: This is an inference about potential limitations.

claim: The enhancement might differ when the APEX molecule is present in different cellular compartments.
source: It is also possible that the enhancement might differ when the APEX molecule is present in different cellular compartments (e.g. cytosol versus endosome lumen).
evidence: This is a speculation about a potential variable.

claim: Variation in gold particle size is dependent on the density of the antigen of interest.
source: However, these issues are dependent on the system being studied; in experiments involving detection of tropomyosin-APEX (Figure 2C–F), gold particles were generally well spaced and well resolved as individual particles and of uniform size (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D). This suggests that variation is dependent on the density of the antigen of interest.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing different experimental systems.

claim: Optimization of the enhancement time is required to allow detection of individual gold particles without formation of single large particles from multiple closely packed APEX molecules.
source: Optimization of the enhancement time is required to allow detection of individual gold particles without formation of single large particles from multiple closely packed APEX molecules.
evidence: This is a stated methodological recommendation.

claim: Careful examination of the labelling pattern for Cavin4 reveals larger particles close to the caveolar membrane, and smaller particles in the neighbouring cytosol.
source: Careful examination of the labelling pattern for Cavin4 reveals larger particles close to the caveolar membrane, and smaller particles in the neighbouring cytosol.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The difference in gold particle size for Cavin4 may be explained by the existence of Cavin4 in different oligomeric states on the caveolar membrane and in the cytosol.
source: This difference in size may be explained by the existence of Cavin4 in different oligomeric states on the caveolar membrane and in the cytosol (Kovtun et al., 2014), that is, it reflects a real biological difference which could be used to infer the state of the protein in particular sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited prior knowledge about Cavin4.

claim: The problem of fused gold particles can potentially be avoided by expressing low levels of APEX-tagged proteins.
source: This problem can potentially be avoided by expressing low levels of APEX-tagged proteins, as shown here for cells expressing an APEX-tagged tropomyosin isoform.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tropomyosin experiments.

claim: The APEX-Gold system is readily compatible with the use of conditionally stabilized APEX-nanobodies to a GFP- or mCherry-tagged protein of interest.
source: However, the system is readily compatible with the use of conditionally stabilized APEX-nanobodies to a GFP- or mCherry-tagged protein of interest as used previously (Ariotti et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of the method and cited prior work.

claim: Using APEX-nanobodies would affect the ability to correlate the APEX-Gold signal with the density of the protein of interest.
source: This would affect the ability to correlate the APEX-Gold signal with the density of the protein of interest but has advantages for CLEM approaches or for detection of protein complexes by using split GFP.
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of using nanobodies.

claim: The APEX-Gold method can provide superior signal-to-noise ratios.
source: Despite these caveats, the APEX-Gold method can provide superior signal-to-noise ratios, allows absolute quantitation of particulate signals, is compatible with 3D EM methods and automated segmentation, and has resolution equal to, or higher than, immunogold labelling.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the advantages of the method.

claim: The APEX-Gold method allows absolute quantitation of particulate signals.
source: Despite these caveats, the APEX-Gold method can provide superior signal-to-noise ratios, allows absolute quantitation of particulate signals, is compatible with 3D EM methods and automated segmentation, and has resolution equal to, or higher than, immunogold labelling.
evidence: This is a summary claim about the advantages of the method.

claim: The APEX-Gold method has resolution equal to, or higher than, immunogold labelling.
source: Despite these caveats, the APEX-Gold method can provide superior signal-to-noise ratios, allows absolute quantitation of particulate signals, is compatible with 3D EM methods and automated segmentation, and has resolution equal to, or higher than, immunogold labelling.
evidence: This is a comparative claim based on the measured resolution data.
